chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who has abundance (of hair), should he part it or leave it? So he (peace be upon him) said: He should part it.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.وَفْرَة: Abundance or fullness, specifically referring to hair in this context
key_terms.يَفْرُقُهَا: He parts it (referring to the hair)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on styling hair for men with abundant hair?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the preferred grooming practice for a man with abundant hair, instructing him to part it rather than leaving it unstyled. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on *Zinah* (adornment) and maintaining a neat, dignified appearance as an act of following the Sunnah of the Imams. It underscores the principle that personal grooming is not merely aesthetic but a religiously endorsed practice that enhances one's presentation in accordance with Islamic etiquette.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas Al Baqbaaq who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who happens to have abundance (of hair), shall he part (style) it or leave it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should part (style) it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn al- Hassan from abu al-‘Abbas al-Baqbaq who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has long hairs: if he must leave them or part them. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must part them.’”
